name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
description: The nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way, located 2.5 million light-years away. SPHEREx monitors the extended disk for variable stars, nova outbursts, and dust emission shifts across 6-month survey passes.
highlight: Repeat observations from July 2025 and July 2026 showing stellar stability and variable sources.

name: Orion Nebula & Molecular Cloud (M42)
description: One of the most active star-forming regions in the local Milky Way. Dense molecular gas, young protostars, and outflow shocks exhibit infrared temporal variations between SPHEREx passes.
highlight: Multi-epoch observations from September 2025 and March 2026 revealing photometric variability in protostellar candidates.

name: Pleiades Cluster (M45)
description: An open star cluster in Taurus containing over 1,000 confirmed stars. Ideal baseline for photometric cross-calibration and tracking fast-moving solar system objects crossing the ecliptic lane.
highlight: Six-month cadence survey passes from August 2025 and February 2026.

name: Galactic Center & Bulge
description: The heart of the Milky Way, obscured in visible light by dust but transparent in SPHEREx near-infrared wavelengths. Contains extreme stellar densities, variable Mira stars, and transient infrared flares.
highlight: Comparing August 2025 and March 2026 near-infrared epochs through deep dust lanes.

name: South Ecliptic Pole Deep Field
description: SPHEREx deep survey convergence zone near the ecliptic pole, visited frequently on every orbital revolution. Yields high signal-to-noise ratio measurements for faint brown dwarfs and distant galaxies.
highlight: Multi-pass integration with repeat observations between April 2025 and July 2026.
